editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the Certified Healthcare Facility Manager exam covering compliance and project management across 110 multiple-choice items.
editorial.overview: The Certified Healthcare Facility Manager certification examination encompasses five major content areas including compliance, healthcare project management, maintenance and operations, finance management, and administration. The American Hospital Association Certification Center conducts this credentialing program to test professional competence, technical knowledge, and operational proficiency in managing modern healthcare facilities across various clinical environments during the 120 minutes allowed.
editorial.who_should_take: Healthcare facility managers, engineering professionals, and supervisors with specified degrees and years of associated engineering and management experience in a healthcare setting qualify to take this certification examination.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Begin your preparation by carefully reviewing the official examination content outline and guidelines provided in the handbook to understand every single tested concept. Complete the self-assessment examination to identify your current knowledge gaps, and study all listed source resources carefully to ensure you are fully prepared for test day success.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses heavily on building codes, safety regulations, and environmental standards that must be strictly met in all accredited healthcare facilities to ensure patient safety and maintain regulatory compliance.
study_focus: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers pre-construction risk assessments, detailed architectural design reviews, and careful construction coordination within complex, active healthcare environments designed to protect both patients and staff members from potential environmental hazards.

This operational domain addresses the safe day-to-day operation and maintenance of building systems, designated utility management programs, and preventive maintenance strategies required in modern hospitals to sustain continuous facility operations without interruption.

This financial domain involves managing operational, construction, capital, and utility budgets while evaluating equipment and service bids to ensure fiscal responsibility and cost effectiveness within the hospital facility department.

This administrative domain deals with departmental administration, routine policy revision, long-range capital improvement planning, and human resource management to maintain high organizational standards across the entire healthcare facility environment.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Report to the PSI test center with proper identification. On-site security rules apply, and calculators are permitted during the 120 minutes allowed for the exam containing 110 questions.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The certification examination is composed of a total of 110 multiple-choice questions designed to test your professional knowledge across all required healthcare facility management domains.
The official examination uses the Modified Angoff method to determine the required passing standard, and the specific minimum passing score is not published in the candidate handbook.
A candidate is allowed exactly 120 minutes, or two full hours, in which to complete the entire examination at authorized PSI test centers located around the world.
The American Hospital Association Certification Center contracts with PSI Services to assist in the development, administration, scoring, score reporting, and security analysis of the examination.
